rule: Use the context-specific safe API, parameterization, encoding, redaction, or fixed allowlist immediately before the sink; never rely on generic input filtering to make a value safe for every context.

contexts.sink: Django HTML templates and browser DOM updates
contexts.treatment: Django contextual auto-escaping remains enabled; JavaScript creates nodes and assigns dynamic text through textContent. Inline script, HTML parsing, code execution, and custom trusted-HTML APIs are prohibited.

contexts.sink: Django ORM and 25 reviewed raw SQL calls
contexts.treatment: Application queries use the Django ORM. The three cursor calls use fixed literal SQL; the two data-bearing calls pass values separately as driver parameters and the readiness query contains no untrusted value. The 22 schema-editor calls execute fixed module-level migration literals and receive no untrusted data.

contexts.sink: Django renderer and template inheritance or inclusion
contexts.treatment: Every renderer and template dependency uses a fixed literal existing template. Runtime template source, dynamic names, and mixed dynamic fallback lists are prohibited.

contexts.sink: Python and Django regular-expression compilation and matching
contexts.treatment: Patterns are fixed literals except for the reviewed password-policy alternation, where every configured word is independently re.escape encoded before insertion into fixed anchored syntax.
The production Python runtime launches no child process and imports no process-launch API. Maintenance orchestration is fixed repository-owned shell or PowerShell outside request handling.

contexts.sink: Python format strings, datetime grammars, logging templates, and percent formatting
contexts.treatment: Format grammars are code-owned literals. The one iterated CSV date parser selects from an exact literal allowlist; dynamic format specifications and runtime string-template grammars are prohibited.

contexts.sink: HTTP redirects and internal notification links
contexts.treatment: Redirects require a same-authority safe URL or an exact configured HTTPS authority. Notification actions accept only local absolute paths with no scheme, authority, or backslash; no second decoding occurs.

contexts.sink: Transaction and audit CSV cells opened by spreadsheet software
contexts.treatment: Every dynamic text cell passes formula_safe_text immediately before csv.writer. Leading whitespace is ignored for detection and values beginning with equals, plus, minus, or at-sign receive a literal-text prefix.

contexts.sink: Operational console and isolated security archive records
contexts.treatment: Messages and field names are code-owned. Context is bounded and pseudonymous; bodies, queries, paths, secrets, financial contents, object IDs, raw exception text, and attacker-controlled log destinations are prohibited.

contexts.sink: Local file open, replace, and verification operations
contexts.treatment: Request users cannot supply a filesystem path. Trusted commands require configured absolute roots or normalize an explicit operator path, reject traversal and symlinks where confidentiality matters, use exclusive opens, and validate a supplied checkpoint name with Path.name equality.

contexts.sink: SMTP, IMAP, or email header construction
contexts.treatment: The initial release sends no email and hardened settings use Django's dummy backend. No user-controlled subject, recipient, address header, or protocol command reaches an email transport.
